verses.1:1: In the days of Ahasuerus, who reigned from India to Ethiopia over one hundred twenty-seven provinces,
verses.1:2: when he sat on the throne of his kingdom, the city of Susa was the beginning of his kingdom.
verses.1:3: Therefore, in the third year of his reign, he held a great banquet for all his princes and attendants, the mightiest of the Persians and the renowned of the Medes, and the governors of the provinces before him,
verses.1:4: so that he might display the riches of the glory of his kingdom, and the greatness and ostentation of his power, for a long time, namely one hundred and eighty days.
verses.1:5: And when the days of the banquet were completed, he invited all the people who were found in Susa, from the greatest to the least, and ordered a banquet to be prepared for seven days in the forecourt of the garden and of the grove that had been planted by royal care and hand.
verses.1:6: And on every side hung canopies of sky-blue, linen, and violet color, held up by cords of fine linen and purple, which had been passed through ivory rings and were supported by marble pillars. Couches of gold and silver were also arranged on a pavement laid with emerald and Parian stone, which painted work adorned with marvelous variety.
verses.1:7: Now those who had been invited drank from golden cups, and foods were brought in on ever-different vessels. Wine also, as was worthy of royal magnificence, was set out abundant and choice.
verses.1:8: Nor was there anyone who compelled those who were unwilling to drink, but it was just as the king had appointed, setting one of his princes over each table so that each person might take what he wanted.
verses.1:9: Queen Vashti also held a banquet for the women in the palace where King Ahasuerus was accustomed to reside.
verses.1:10: And so on the seventh day, when the king was quite merry and after excessive drinking had grown warm with unmixed wine, he commanded Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas, the seven eunuchs who served in his presence,
verses.1:11: to bring Queen Vashti before the king, with the diadem placed on her head, so that he might display her beauty to all the peoples and princes, for she was exceedingly beautiful.
verses.1:12: But she refused, and disdained to come at the king's command that he had sent through the eunuchs. At this the king, angry and inflamed with excessive fury,
verses.1:13: questioned the wise men who by royal custom were always at his side, and by whose counsel he did all things, men who knew the laws and ordinances of the ancestors
verses.1:14: (now the foremost and closest were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seven leaders of the Persians and of the Medes, who saw the king's face and were accustomed to sit first after him),
verses.1:15: as to what sentence Queen Vashti should be subject to, because she had refused to carry out the command of King Ahasuerus that he had sent through the eunuchs.
verses.1:16: And Memucan answered in the hearing of the king and the princes, "Not only has Queen Vashti wronged the king, but also all the peoples and princes who are in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus.
verses.1:17: For the report of the queen will go out to all women, so that they will despise their husbands and say, 'King Ahasuerus ordered Queen Vashti to come in to him, and she refused.'
verses.1:18: And by this example all the wives of the princes of the Persians and of the Medes will think little of the commands of their husbands; therefore the indignation of the king is just.
verses.1:19: If it pleases you, let an edict go out from your presence, and let it be written according to the law of the Persians and of the Medes, which it is unlawful to transgress, that Vashti may never again come in to the king, but that another who is better than she may receive her kingdom.
verses.1:20: And let this be published throughout the entire empire of your provinces (which is vast), and let all wives, both of the greater and of the lesser, give honor to their husbands."
verses.1:21: His counsel pleased the king and the princes, and the king acted according to the counsel of Memucan,
verses.1:22: and sent letters to all the provinces of his kingdom, as each people was able to hear and read, in various languages and scripts, that men are the rulers and superiors in their own houses, and that this should be published among all the peoples.
verses.2:1: When these things had been done in this way, after the indignation of King Ahasuerus had subsided, he remembered Vashti, and what she had done or what she had suffered.
verses.2:2: And the king's attendants and his ministers said, "Let attractive young women who are virgins be sought for the king,
verses.2:3: and let men be sent to look out throughout all the provinces for attractive young women who are virgins, and let them bring them to the city of Susa and hand them over into the house of the women under the hand of Hegai the eunuch, who is overseer and keeper of the royal women; and let them receive women's cosmetics and the other things necessary for their use.
verses.2:4: And whichever one among them all pleases the eyes of the king, let her reign in place of Vashti." The word pleased the king, and he ordered it to be done just as they had suggested.
verses.2:5: There was a Jewish man in the city of Susa, named Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, of the lineage of Jemini,
verses.2:6: who had been carried away from Jerusalem at the time when Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had carried away Jeconiah, king of Judah,
verses.2:7: who was the foster father of his brother's daughter Hadassah, who by another name was called Esther and had lost both parents; she was exceedingly beautiful and graceful in appearance. And when her father and mother had died, Mordecai adopted her for himself as a daughter.
verses.2:8: And when the king's command had spread abroad, and according to his order many beautiful virgins were being brought to Susa and handed over to Hegai the eunuch, Esther also among the other young women was handed over to him to be kept in the number of the women.
verses.2:9: And she pleased him and found favor in his sight. And he commanded a eunuch to hasten the women's cosmetics, and to give her her portions and seven most attractive young women from the king's house, and to adorn and care for both her and her maidservants.
verses.2:10: She was unwilling to disclose to him her people and her homeland, for Mordecai had commanded her to remain completely silent about this matter.
verses.2:11: And he walked about daily in front of the forecourt of the house in which the chosen virgins were kept, caring for the welfare of Esther and wanting to know what would happen to her.
verses.2:12: Now when the time came for each young woman in turn to go in to the king, after everything that pertained to women's adornment had been completed, the twelfth month was coming around; specifically in this way, that for six months they were anointed with oil of myrrh, and for the other six they used certain ointments and spices.
verses.2:13: And when going in to the king, they received whatever they had asked for pertaining to attire; and dressed just as it had pleased them, they passed from the hall of the women to the king's chamber.
verses.2:14: And the one who had gone in at evening went out in the morning, and from there was led away into the second house, which was under the hand of Shaashgaz the eunuch, who presided over the king's concubines; nor did she have authority to return to the king any longer, unless the king wished it and ordered her to come by name.
verses.2:15: Now when the time had elapsed in turn, the day was approaching on which Esther, the daughter of Abihail the brother of Mordecai, whom he had adopted for himself as a daughter, was to go in to the king. She did not seek women's adornment, but whatever Hegai the eunuch, the keeper of the virgins, wanted, these things he gave her for attire. For she was exceedingly lovely and of incredible beauty; to the eyes of all she appeared gracious and lovable.
verses.2:16: Therefore she was led to the chamber of King Ahasuerus in the tenth month, which is called Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.
verses.2:17: And the king loved her deeply, more than all the women, and she had favor and mercy before him above all the women; and he placed the diadem of the kingdom on her head and made her reign in place of Vashti.
verses.2:18: And he ordered a most magnificent banquet to be prepared for all his princes and servants for the union and wedding of Esther. And he gave rest to all the provinces, and bestowed gifts generously according to sovereign magnificence.
verses.2:19: And when virgins were sought and gathered a second time, Mordecai remained at the king's gate.
verses.2:20: Esther had not yet disclosed her homeland and her people, according to his order. For whatever he commanded, Esther observed; and she did all things just as she had been accustomed at the time when he was raising her as a little girl.
verses.2:21: Therefore, at that time when Mordecai was staying at the king's gate, Bigthan and Teresh, two eunuchs of the king who were gatekeepers and presided at the first threshold of the palace, became angry and wanted to rise up against the king and kill him.
verses.2:22: This was not hidden from Mordecai, and immediately he reported it to Queen Esther, and she to the king in the name of Mordecai, who had brought the matter to her.
verses.2:23: It was investigated and found out, and each of them was hanged on a gallows. And it was committed to the histories and handed over to the annals before the king.
verses.3:1: After these things King Ahasuerus exalted Haman the son of Hammedatha, who was of the lineage of Agag, and placed his throne above all the princes whom he had.
verses.3:2: And all the king's servants who stayed at the doors of the palace bent their knees and paid homage to Haman, for so the emperor had commanded them; Mordecai alone did not bend the knee or pay homage to him.
verses.3:3: And the king's attendants who presided at the doors of the palace said to him, "Why, unlike the others, do you not observe the king's order?"
verses.3:4: And when they said this repeatedly and he was unwilling to listen, they reported it to Haman, desiring to know whether he would persist in his resolve; for he had told them that he was a Jew.
verses.3:5: When Haman heard this, and had verified by experience that Mordecai did not bend the knee to him or pay homage to him, he became exceedingly angry,
verses.3:6: and he counted it as nothing to lay his hands on Mordecai alone, for he had heard that he was of the Jewish people; and instead he wanted to destroy the entire nation of the Jews who were in the kingdom of Ahasuerus.
verses.3:7: In the first month (whose name is Nisan), in the twelfth year of the reign of Ahasuerus, a lot, which in Hebrew is called Pur, was cast into an urn before Haman, as to what day and what month the Jewish people should be killed; and the twelfth month came out, which is called Adar.
verses.3:8: And Haman said to King Ahasuerus, "There is a people scattered throughout all the provinces of your kingdom and separated from one another, using new laws and ceremonies, and moreover despising the decrees of the king; and you know very well that it is not advantageous for your kingdom for it to grow insolent through license.
verses.3:9: If it pleases you, decree that it perish, and I will weigh out ten thousand talents to the treasurers of your treasury."
verses.3:10: Therefore the king took the ring that he used from his hand and gave it to Haman the son of Hammedatha, of the offspring of Agag, the enemy of the Jews,
verses.3:11: and said to him, "Let the silver that you promise be yours; with the people, do what pleases you."
verses.3:12: And the king's scribes were summoned in the first month, Nisan, on the thirteenth day of the same month; and it was written, as Haman had ordered, to all the satraps of the king, and to the judges of the provinces and of the various peoples, as each people was able to read and hear according to the variety of their languages, in the name of King Ahasuerus; and the letters, sealed with his own ring,
verses.3:13: were sent by the king's couriers to all the provinces, that they should kill and wipe out all the Jews, from boy to old man, little children and women, on one day, that is, the thirteenth of the twelfth month, which is called Adar, and plunder their goods.
verses.3:14: Now the summary of the letters was this: that all the provinces should know and prepare themselves for the day named beforehand.
verses.3:15: The couriers who had been sent hurried to carry out the king's command. And immediately the edict was hung up in Susa, while the king and Haman were celebrating a banquet and all the Jews who were in the city were weeping.
verses.4:1: When Mordecai heard these things, he tore his garments and clothed himself in sackcloth, scattering ashes on his head; and in the square in the middle of the city he was crying out with a loud voice, showing the bitterness of his spirit,
verses.4:2: and walking with this wailing as far as the gates of the palace. For it was not permitted for one clothed in sackcloth to enter the king's court.
verses.4:3: Also in all the provinces, towns, and places to which the king's cruel decree had come, there was immense mourning among the Jews, fasting, wailing, and weeping, with many using sackcloth and ashes for a bed.
verses.4:4: Now Esther's maids and eunuchs came in and reported it to her. Hearing this, she was dismayed, and she sent clothing so that, once the sackcloth was removed, they might clothe him; but he refused to accept it.
verses.4:5: Then, having summoned Hathach the eunuch, whom the king had given to her as an attendant, she commanded him to go to Mordecai and learn from him why he was doing this.
verses.4:6: And Hathach went out to Mordecai, who was standing in the square of the city, in front of the palace entrance:
verses.4:7: He disclosed to him everything that had happened: how Haman had promised to bring silver into the king's treasuries for the slaughter of the Jews.
verses.4:8: He also gave him a copy of the edict that was hanging in Susa, so that he might show it to the queen and urge her to go in to the king and plead with him for her people.
verses.4:9: Hathach returned and reported to Esther everything that Mordecai had said.
verses.4:10: She answered him and ordered him to say to Mordecai:
verses.4:11: "All the king's servants and all the provinces that are under his dominion know that whether a man or a woman enters the inner courtyard of the king without being called, he is to be put to death immediately without any delay, unless perhaps the king extends the golden scepter toward him as a sign of clemency, and so he may be able to live. How then will I be able to go in to the king, who for thirty days now have not been called to him?"
verses.4:13: he sent word to Esther again, saying, "Do not think that you will save your life alone because you are in the king's house above all the Jews;
verses.4:14: for if you remain silent now, the Jews will be saved through another opportunity, and you and your father's house will perish. And who knows whether you have come to the kingdom for this reason, that you might be prepared at such a time?"
verses.4:15: And Esther again sent these words to Mordecai:
verses.4:16: "Go and gather all the Jews whom you find in Susa, and pray for me. Do not eat and do not drink for three days and three nights; and I with my maidservants will fast in the same way, and then I will go in to the king, acting against the law, without being called, and handing myself over to death and danger."
verses.4:17: So Mordecai went and did everything that Esther had commanded him.
verses.5:1: Now on the third day Esther clothed herself in royal garments and stood in the courtyard of the royal house, which was the inner one, opposite the king's hall; while he was sitting upon his throne in the council chamber of the palace opposite the entrance of the house.
verses.5:2: And when he saw Queen Esther standing, she pleased his eyes, and he extended toward her the golden scepter that he held in his hand; and she approached and kissed the tip of his scepter.
verses.5:3: And the king said to her, "What do you wish, Queen Esther? What is your petition? Even if you ask for half of the kingdom, it will be given to you."
verses.5:4: And she answered, "If it pleases the king, I implore you to come to me today, and Haman with you, to the banquet that I have prepared."
verses.5:5: And immediately the king said, "Call Haman quickly, so that he may obey Esther's will." So the king and Haman came to the banquet that the queen had prepared for them.
verses.5:6: And the king said to her, after he had drunk wine abundantly, "What do you ask to be given to you? And for what matter are you making a request? Even if you ask for half of my kingdom, you will obtain it."
verses.5:7: Esther answered him, "My petition and pleas are these:
verses.5:8: if I have found favor in the sight of the king, and if it pleases the king to give me what I request and to fulfill my petition, let the king and Haman come to the banquet that I have prepared for them, and tomorrow I will reveal my will to the king."
verses.5:9: So Haman went out on that day glad and cheerful. And when he saw Mordecai sitting before the gates of the palace, and saw that he not only did not rise for him, but did not even move from the place where he was sitting, he was greatly indignant;
verses.5:10: and, concealing his anger, he returned to his house and called together to himself his friends and Zeresh his wife,
verses.5:11: and recounted to them the greatness of his riches, and the multitude of his sons, and with how much glory the king had elevated him above all his princes and servants.
verses.5:12: And after these things he said, "Queen Esther also invited no one else to the banquet with the king except me; and tomorrow also I am going to dine with her along with the king.
verses.5:13: And although I have all these things, I think I have nothing as long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting before the royal gates."
verses.5:14: And Zeresh his wife and his other friends answered him, "Order a tall beam to be prepared, having a height of fifty cubits, and tell the king in the morning that Mordecai should be hanged on it, and so you will go gladly with the king to the banquet." The advice pleased him, and he ordered a tall cross to be prepared.
verses.6:1: The king spent that night sleepless, and he ordered the histories and annals of former times to be brought to him. While these were being read in his presence,
verses.6:2: they came to that place where it was written how Mordecai had reported the plot of Bigthan and Teresh, the eunuchs, who desired to murder King Ahasuerus.
verses.6:3: When the king heard this, he said, "What honor and reward has Mordecai obtained for this loyalty?" His servants and attendants said to him, "He has received no recompense at all."
verses.6:4: And immediately the king said, "Who is in the courtyard?" For Haman had entered the inner courtyard of the royal house to suggest to the king that he order Mordecai to be fastened to the gallows that had been prepared for him.
verses.6:5: The young servants answered, "Haman is standing in the courtyard." And the king said, "Let him come in."
verses.6:6: And when he had come in, he said to him, "What ought to be done for the man whom the king desires to honor?" Now Haman, thinking in his heart and considering that the king wished to honor no one else except himself,
verses.6:7: answered, "The man whom the king desires to honor,
verses.6:8: ought to be clothed in royal garments, and be placed upon a horse that is of the king's saddle, and receive the royal diadem upon his head;
verses.6:9: and let the foremost of the royal princes and rulers hold his horse, and walking through the square of the city, let him cry out and say, 'Thus will anyone be honored whom the king wishes to honor.'"
verses.6:10: And the king said to him, "Hurry, and having taken the robe and the horse, do, as you have spoken, for Mordecai the Jew, who sits before the gates of the palace. Be careful not to omit any of these things that you have spoken."
verses.6:11: So Haman took the robe and the horse, and in the square of the city he walked ahead of Mordecai, who had been clothed and placed upon the horse, and cried out, "Worthy of this honor is anyone whom the king wishes to honor."
verses.6:12: And Mordecai returned to the gate of the palace, and Haman hurried to go to his house, mourning and with his head covered;
verses.6:13: and he told Zeresh his wife and his friends everything that had happened to him. The wise men whom he had in counsel, and his wife, answered him, "If Mordecai, before whom you have begun to fall, is of the seed of the Jews, you will not be able to resist him, but you will fall in his sight."
verses.6:14: While they were still speaking, the king's eunuchs came and compelled him to proceed quickly to the banquet that the queen had prepared.
verses.7:1: So the king and Haman went in to drink with the queen.
verses.7:2: And the king said to her on the second day as well, after he had grown warm with wine, "What is your petition, Esther, that it may be given to you? And what do you want to be done? Even if you ask for half of my kingdom, you will obtain it."
verses.7:3: To him she answered, "If I have found favor in your eyes, king, and if it pleases you, grant me my life, for which I ask, and my people, for whom I plead.
verses.7:4: For we have been handed over, I and my people, to be crushed, to be slaughtered, and to perish. And if only we were being sold as male slaves and female slaves: it would be a bearable evil, and, groaning, I would keep silent; but now our foe is one whose cruelty rebounds upon the king."
verses.7:5: And King Ahasuerus answered and said, "Who is this man, and of what power is he, that he dares to do these things?"
verses.7:6: And Esther said, "Our worst foe and enemy is this Haman." Hearing this, he was immediately stunned, unable to bear the face of the king and the queen.
verses.7:7: Then the king rose up in anger, and from the place of the banquet went into the garden planted with trees. Haman also rose up to beg Queen Esther for his life, for he understood that evil had been prepared for him by the king.
verses.7:8: When he had returned from the garden planted with groves and had entered the place of the banquet, he found that Haman had fallen upon the couch on which Esther was lying, and he said, "He even wants to assault the queen, with me present, in my house!" The word had not yet gone out from the mouth of the king, and immediately they covered his face.
verses.7:9: And Harbona, one of the eunuchs who stood in the service of the king, said, "Look, the timber that he had prepared for Mordecai, who spoke for the king, stands in the house of Haman, having a height of fifty cubits." To him the king said, "Hang him on it."
verses.7:10: So Haman was hanged on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai, and the king's anger subsided.
verses.8:1: On that day King Ahasuerus gave to Queen Esther the house of Haman, the adversary of the Jews, and Mordecai entered before the face of the king. For Esther had confessed to him that he was her uncle.
verses.8:2: And the king took the ring that he had ordered to be taken back from Haman, and delivered it to Mordecai. And Esther appointed Mordecai over her house.
verses.8:3: And not content with these things, she fell down at the feet of the king, wept, and speaking to him, implored that he would command the malice of Haman the Agagite and his most wicked schemes, which he had devised against the Jews, to be made void.
verses.8:4: But he, according to custom, extended the golden scepter with his hand, by which a sign of clemency was shown; and rising up, she stood before him,
verses.8:5: and said, "If it pleases the king, and if I have found favor in his eyes, and my plea does not seem contrary to him, I plead that by new letters the old letters of Haman, the plotter and foe of the Jews, by which he had commanded them to perish in all the provinces of the king, may be corrected.
verses.8:6: For how will I be able to endure the slaughter and killing of my people?"
verses.8:7: And King Ahasuerus answered Queen Esther and Mordecai the Jew, "I have granted the house of Haman to Esther, and I have ordered him to be fastened to a cross, because he dared to lay a hand on the Jews.
verses.8:8: Write therefore to the Jews, as it pleases you, in the king's name, sealing the letters with my ring." For this was the custom, that no one would dare to contradict letters that were sent in the king's name and were sealed with his ring.
verses.8:9: And when the scribes and copyists of the king had been summoned (now it was the time of the third month, which is called Sivan), on its twenty-third day letters were written, as Mordecai had desired, to the Jews, and to the princes, governors, and judges who presided over the one hundred and twenty-seven provinces from India as far as Ethiopia, to province after province and to people after people according to their languages and scripts, and to the Jews, just as they were able to read and hear.
verses.8:10: And the letters themselves, which were sent in the king's name, were sealed with his ring and sent by couriers, who, speeding through all the provinces, were to forestall the old letters with new messages.
verses.8:11: The king commanded them to meet with the Jews in each city and order them to gather together into one, so that they might stand for their lives, and kill and destroy all their enemies, with their wives and children and all their households, and plunder their spoils.
verses.8:12: And one day of vengeance was appointed throughout all the provinces, that is, the thirteenth of the twelfth month, Adar.
verses.8:13: And the summary of the letter was this: that in all lands and peoples that were subject to the rule of King Ahasuerus, it should be made known that the Jews were ready to take vengeance on their foes.
verses.8:14: And the swift couriers went out carrying the messages, and the king's edict hung in Susa.
verses.8:15: Now Mordecai, going out from the palace and from the presence of the king, shone in royal garments, namely violet and sky-blue, wearing a golden crown on his head and wrapped in a cloak of silk and purple. And the entire city exulted and rejoiced.
verses.8:16: But for the Jews a new light seemed to rise: joy, honor, and jubilation.
verses.8:17: Among all peoples, cities, and provinces, wherever the king's orders came, there was marvelous exultation, feasts and banquets, and a festive day, to such an extent that many of another nation and sect joined themselves to their religion and ceremonies. For a great terror of the Jewish name had seized everyone.
verses.9:1: Therefore, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which we have already said before is called Adar, when killing was being prepared for all the Jews and their foes were craving blood, in reversal the Jews began to prevail and to avenge themselves on their adversaries.
verses.9:2: And they gathered together in each city, town, and place to stretch out a hand against their enemies and persecutors. And no one dared to resist, because dread of their greatness had penetrated all peoples.
verses.9:3: For even the judges of the provinces, and the commanders, and the governors, and every dignitary who presided over each place and work, exalted the Jews out of fear of Mordecai,
verses.9:4: whom they knew to be the prince of the palace and to have very great power; the fame of his name also grew daily and flew through the mouths of all.
verses.9:5: Therefore, the Jews struck their enemies with a great blow and killed them, repaying them for what they had prepared to do to them:
verses.9:6: to such an extent that even in Susa they killed five hundred men, besides the ten sons of Haman the Agagite, foe of the Jews, whose names are these:
verses.9:8: and Poratha, and Adalia, and Aridatha,
verses.9:9: and Parmashta, and Arisai, and Aridai, and Jezatha.
verses.9:10: When they had killed them, they refused to touch plunder from their possessions.
verses.9:11: And immediately the number of those who had been killed in Susa was reported to the king.
verses.9:12: He said to the queen, "In the city of Susa the Jews have killed five hundred men, and ten others, the sons of Haman; how great a slaughter do you think they are carrying out in all the provinces? What further do you ask, and what do you want me to command to be done?"
verses.9:13: To him she answered, "If it pleases the king, let authority be given to the Jews that just as they have done today in Susa, so they may also do tomorrow, and let the ten sons of Haman be hanged on gallows."
verses.9:14: And the king commanded that it be done so. And immediately the edict hung in Susa, and the ten sons of Haman were hanged.
verses.9:15: When the Jews had gathered together on the fourteenth day of the month of Adar, three hundred men were killed in Susa, nor was their property plundered by them.
verses.9:16: Moreover, throughout all the provinces that were subject to the dominion of the king, the Jews stood for their lives, having killed their foes and persecutors, to such an extent that the number of those killed reached seventy-five thousand, and no one touched anything from their possessions.
verses.9:17: Now the thirteenth day of the month of Adar was the first day of killing among all of them, and on the fourteenth day they ceased to slaughter. That day they appointed to be a solemn day, so that on it, at all times thereafter, they might devote themselves to feasts, joy, and banquets.
verses.9:18: But those who had carried out the slaughter in the city of Susa were engaged in slaughter on the thirteenth and fourteenth day of the same month; on the fifteenth day, however, they ceased to strike. And therefore they appointed that same day as a solemn day of feasts and gladness.
verses.9:19: Those Jews, however, who lived in unwalled towns and villages decreed the fourteenth day of the month of Adar as a day of banquets and joy, so that they exult on it and send one another portions of feasts and food.
verses.9:20: So Mordecai wrote all these things, and, set down in writing, sent them to the Jews who lived in all the provinces of the king, both those situated nearby and those far away,
verses.9:21: that they should accept the fourteenth and fifteenth day of the month of Adar as feast days, and, as the year always returns, celebrate them with solemn honor,
verses.9:22: because on those very days the Jews avenged themselves on their enemies, and mourning and sorrow were turned into cheerfulness and joy; and that these days should be days of feasts and gladness, and that they should send one another portions of food and bestow small gifts upon the poor.
verses.9:23: And the Jews accepted as a solemn rite all that they had begun to do at that time, and what Mordecai had commanded in letters to be done.
verses.9:24: For Haman, son of Hammedatha of the lineage of Agag, foe and adversary of the Jews, plotted evil against them, to kill and destroy them; and he cast Pur, which in our language is translated as lot.
verses.9:25: And afterward Esther went in to the king, pleading that his attempts might be made void by the king's letters, and that the evil which he had plotted against the Jews might return upon his head. Finally, they fastened both him and his sons to a cross,
verses.9:26: and from that time these days were called Purim, that is, of lots, because Pur, that is, the lot, had been cast into the urn. And all the things that were done are contained in the scroll of this letter, that is, of this book:
verses.9:27: and what they endured, and what was afterward changed, the Jews took upon themselves and their seed, and upon all who wished to be joined to their religion, so that no one is permitted to pass these two days without solemn observance, which the writing attests and fixed times require, as the years continually succeed one another.
verses.9:28: These are the days that no oblivion will ever blot out, and throughout every generation all provinces in the entire world will celebrate them; nor is there any city in which the days of Purim, that is, of lots, are not observed by the Jews and by their progeny, which is bound by these ceremonies.
verses.9:29: And Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew wrote a second letter as well, so that with all diligence this solemn day might be ratified for the future:
verses.9:30: and they sent it to all the Jews who lived in the one hundred twenty-seven provinces of King Ahasuerus, so that they might have peace and accept the truth,
verses.9:31: observing the days of lots, and that they should celebrate them in their proper time with joy, just as Mordecai and Esther had appointed; and they accepted to be observed by themselves and by their seed the fasts, and the cries, and the days of lots,
verses.9:32: and all things that are contained in the history of this book, which is called Esther.
verses.10:1: Now King Ahasuerus made the entire land and all the islands of the sea subject to tribute.
verses.10:2: His might and dominion, and the honor and eminence with which he exalted Mordecai, are written in the books of the Medes and Persians,
verses.10:3: and how Mordecai, of Jewish descent, was second to King Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and pleasing to the populace of his brothers, seeking good things for his people and speaking the things that pertained to the peace of his seed.
verses.10:4: And Mordecai said, "These things have been done by God.
verses.10:5: I remembered the dream that I had seen, which signified these same things, and not one of them was in vain.
verses.10:6: The little spring, which grew into a river, and was turned into light and the sun, and overflowed into abundant waters, is Esther, whom the king took as a wife and willed to be queen.
verses.10:7: Now the two dragons are I and Haman.
verses.10:8: The nations that had assembled are those who attempted to blot out the name of the Jews.
verses.10:9: But my nation is Israel, which cried out to the Lord, and the Lord saved His people; and He freed us from all evils and performed great signs and wonders among the nations;
verses.10:10: and He commanded that there be two lots, one for the people of God, and the other for all the nations.
verses.10:11: And each of the two lots came to the day already fixed from that time before God for all the nations,
verses.10:12: and the Lord remembered His people and showed mercy to His inheritance.
verses.10:13: And these days will be observed in the month of Adar on the fourteenth and fifteenth day of the same month, with all eagerness and joy, in one assembly of the gathered people, for all succeeding generations of the people of Israel."
verses.11:1: In the fourth year, while Ptolemy and Cleopatra were reigning, Dositheus, who claimed to be a priest and of Levitical descent, and Ptolemy his son brought this letter of Purim, which they said Lysimachus the son of Ptolemy had translated in Jerusalem.
verses.11:2: In the second year, while Artaxerxes the Great was reigning, on the first day of the month of Nisan, Mordecai the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, of the tribe of Benjamin, saw a dream:
verses.11:3: a Jewish man who lived in the city of Susa, a great man and among the foremost of the royal court.
verses.11:4: Now he was of that number of captives whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away from Jerusalem with Jeconiah king of Judah.
verses.11:5: And this was his dream: voices appeared, and tumults, and thunderings, and earthquakes, and turmoil upon the earth;
verses.11:6: and look, two great dragons, ready for battle against each other.
verses.11:7: At their cry all the nations were stirred up to fight against the nation of the righteous.
verses.11:8: And that day was a day of darkness and peril, of tribulation and distress, and great dread upon the earth.
verses.11:9: And the nation of the righteous was thrown into turmoil, fearing their own evils, and prepared for death.
verses.11:10: And they cried out to God; and as they cried aloud, a little spring grew into a very great river and overflowed into abundant waters.
verses.11:11: Light and the sun rose, and the humble were exalted and devoured the renowned.
verses.11:12: When Mordecai had seen this and had risen from his bed, he pondered what God intended to do; and he held it fixed in his mind, desiring to know what the dream signified.
verses.12:1: Now at that time he was staying in the king's court with Bagatha and Thara, eunuchs of the king, who were doorkeepers of the palace.
verses.12:2: And when he had understood their thoughts and examined their schemes more carefully, he learned that they were attempting to lay hands on King Artaxerxes, and he reported it to the king.
verses.12:3: And when an inquiry had been held concerning both of them, after they confessed, he ordered them to be led away to death.
verses.12:4: Now the king wrote what had happened in the records; and Mordecai also committed the memory of the event to writing.
verses.12:5: And the king commanded him to stay in the court of the palace, having given him gifts for the disclosure.
verses.12:6: But Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Bugaean, was most highly honored before the king, and he wanted to harm Mordecai and his people because of the two eunuchs of the king who had been put to death. And they plundered their goods, or possessions. Now this was the copy of the letter:
verses.13:1: "The greatest King Artaxerxes, from India to Ethiopia, to the princes and leaders of the one hundred twenty-seven provinces who are subject to his dominion: greeting.
verses.13:2: Although I ruled over very many nations and had subjected the entire world to my authority, I wished by no means to abuse the greatness of my power, but to govern my subjects with clemency and gentleness, so that, passing their life in quietness without any terror, they might enjoy the peace desired by all mortals.
verses.13:3: Now when I asked my counselors how this might be accomplished, one who surpassed the rest in wisdom and loyalty, and was second after the king, Haman by name,
verses.13:4: informed me that throughout the whole world a people is scattered who make use of strange laws, and, acting contrary to the custom of all nations, despise the commands of kings, and violate the harmony of all nations by their dissension.
verses.13:5: Having learned this, seeing that one rebellious nation against the entire human race makes use of perverse laws, opposes our commands, and disturbs the peace and harmony of the provinces subject to us,
verses.13:6: we have commanded that all whom Haman, who is set over all the provinces and is second to the king, and whom we honor in the place of a father, points out shall be destroyed with their wives and children by their enemies, and that no one have pity on them, on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month, Adar, of the present year,
verses.13:7: so that these wicked men, going down to the underworld in a single day, may restore to our empire the peace that they had disturbed." And Mordecai went and did everything that Esther had commanded him.
verses.13:8: Now Mordecai implored the Lord, mindful of all His works,
verses.13:9: and he said, "Lord, Lord, almighty King, for in Your authority all things are placed, and there is no one who can resist Your will, if You have decreed to save Israel.
verses.13:10: You made heaven and earth, and whatever is contained within the compass of heaven.
verses.13:11: You are Lord of all, and there is no one who resists Your majesty.
verses.13:12: You know all things, and You know that it was not out of pride and insolence, or any desire for glory, that I did this, refusing to bow down before the most proud Haman
verses.13:13: (for I would willingly be ready to kiss even the footprints of his feet for the salvation of Israel),
verses.13:14: but I feared that I might transfer the honor of my God to a man, and that I might worship anyone except my God.
verses.13:15: And now, Lord King, God of Abraham, have mercy on Your people, because our enemies wish to destroy us and to wipe out Your inheritance.
verses.13:16: Do not despise Your portion, which You redeemed for Yourself out of Egypt.
verses.13:17: Hear my entreaty, and be gracious to Your lot and Your allotted portion, and turn our mourning into joy, so that living we may praise Your name, Lord; and do not close the mouths of those who sing to You."
verses.13:18: All Israel also cried out to the Lord with like mind and supplication, because certain death hung over them.
verses.14:1: Queen Esther also fled for refuge to the Lord, dreading the danger that was impending.
verses.14:2: And when she had laid aside her royal garments, she put on clothing suited for weeping and mourning; and instead of various perfumes, she filled her head with ashes and dung, and humbled her body with fastings; and all the places in which she had previously been accustomed to rejoice, she filled with the tearing of her hair.
verses.14:3: And she implored the Lord God of Israel, saying, "My Lord, who alone are our King, help me who am alone, and who have no other helper besides You.
verses.14:4: My peril is in my hands.
verses.14:5: I have heard from my father that You, Lord, took Israel from all the nations, and our fathers from all their ancestors before them, so that You might possess an everlasting inheritance, and You did for them just as You spoke.
verses.14:6: We have sinned in Your sight, and for that reason You have handed us over into the hands of our enemies,
verses.14:7: for we worshiped their gods. You are righteous, Lord;
verses.14:8: and now it is not enough for them that they oppress us with the harshest servitude, but ascribing the strength of their hands to the power of idols,
verses.14:9: they wish to alter Your promises, and to blot out Your inheritance, and to close the mouths of those who praise You, and to extinguish the glory of Your temple and altar,
verses.14:10: so that they may open the mouths of the nations, and praise the might of idols, and proclaim a fleshly king forever.
verses.14:11: Do not hand over Your scepter, Lord, to those who are not, so that they do not laugh at our ruin; but turn their counsel back upon them, and destroy the one who has begun to rage against us.
verses.14:12: Remember, Lord, and show Yourself to us in the time of our tribulation, and give me confidence, Lord, King of gods and of all power;
verses.14:13: put well-ordered speech in my mouth in the sight of the lion, and turn his heart to hatred of our enemy, so that both he himself and the others who agree with him may perish.
verses.14:14: But deliver us by Your hand, and help me, who have no other help except You, Lord, who have knowledge of all things,
verses.14:15: and You know that I hate the glory of the wicked, and detest the bed of the uncircumcised and of every foreigner.
verses.14:16: You know my necessity, that I abhor the sign of my pride and glory, which is upon my head in the days of my public display, and detest it like a menstruous cloth, and do not wear it in the days of my seclusion,
verses.14:17: and that I have not eaten at Haman's table, nor has the king's banquet pleased me, and I have not drunk the wine of drink offerings;
verses.14:18: and Your maidservant has never rejoiced from the time I was brought here until the present day, except in You, Lord God of Abraham.
verses.14:19: God, mighty above all, hear the voice of those who have no other hope, and deliver us from the hand of the wicked, and rescue me from my fear."
verses.15:1: And he commanded her (no doubt it was Mordecai) to go in to the king and plead for her people and for her homeland.
verses.15:2: "Remember," he said, "the days of your lowliness, how you were nourished by my hand, because Haman, who is second to the king, has spoken against us for death;
verses.15:3: and you, call upon the Lord, and speak to the king for us, and deliver us from death."
verses.15:4: Now on the third day she laid aside her garments of adornment and was clothed with her glory.
verses.15:5: And when she shone in royal attire and had called upon God, the ruler and savior of all, she took two maids,
verses.15:6: and she leaned upon one indeed, as though, because of luxury and excessive delicacy, she could not bear to support her own body;
verses.15:7: while the other of the maids followed her mistress, holding up the garments that flowed down to the ground.
verses.15:8: She herself, with her face suffused with a rosy color and with charming and shining eyes, concealed a sorrowful mind contracted with extreme fear.
verses.15:9: Having therefore entered all the doors in order, she stood opposite the king, where he sat upon the throne of his kingdom, clothed in royal garments and shining with gold and precious stones; and he was terrifying in appearance.
verses.15:10: And when he had lifted his face and with blazing eyes had revealed the fury of his breast, the queen collapsed, and with her color changed to paleness, she leaned her weary head upon the little maid.
verses.15:11: And God turned the spirit of the king into gentleness, and in haste and fear he leaped down from his throne, and supporting her in his arms until she came back to herself, he soothed her with these words:
verses.15:12: "What is the matter with you, Esther? I am your brother; do not be afraid.
verses.15:13: You will not die, for this law was established not for you, but for all.
verses.15:14: Come near therefore, and touch the scepter."
verses.15:15: And when she remained silent, he took the golden scepter and placed it upon her neck, and kissed her, and said, "Why do you not speak to me?"
verses.15:16: And she answered, "I saw you, my lord, like an angel of God, and my heart was thrown into turmoil for fear of your glory.
verses.15:17: For you are very wonderful, my lord, and your face is full of graces."
verses.15:18: And while she was speaking, she collapsed again and nearly fainted away.
verses.15:19: Now the king was distressed, and all his attendants were comforting her.
verses.16:1: "The great King Artaxerxes, from India to Ethiopia, to the leaders and princes of the one hundred twenty-seven provinces who obey our command, sends greeting.
verses.16:2: Many have abused the goodness of princes and the honor that was conferred upon them into pride;
verses.16:3: and not only do they strive to oppress those subject to kings, but not enduring the glory given to them, they plot ambushes against the very ones who gave it.
verses.16:4: Nor are they content not to give thanks for kindnesses and to violate the laws of humanity within themselves, but they even suppose that they can escape the sentence of God, who sees all things.
verses.16:5: And they have broken out into such madness that they attempt to undermine by tunnels of lies those who diligently keep the offices entrusted to them and conduct everything so as to be worthy of everyone's praise,
verses.16:6: while with clever deceit they deceive the simple ears of princes who judge others from their own nature.
verses.16:7: And this matter is proved both from ancient histories and from the things that take place daily, how the aims of kings are corrupted by the evil suggestions of certain men.
verses.16:8: For this reason, provision must be made for the peace of all the provinces.
verses.16:9: Nor ought you to think, if we give different commands, that this comes from the fickleness of our mind, but that we pass judgment according to the character and necessity of the times, as the welfare of the commonwealth demands.
verses.16:10: And so that you may understand more clearly what we say: Haman the son of Hammedatha, a Macedonian in both spirit and nation, and alien to the blood of the Persians, and staining our goodness with his cruelty, was received by us as a foreigner,
verses.16:11: and experienced such great kindness toward himself that he was called our father, and was bowed down to by all as second after the king;
verses.16:12: who was lifted up into such a swelling of arrogance that he strove to deprive us of both kingdom and breath.
verses.16:13: For by certain new and unheard-of schemes he sought to bring to death Mordecai, by whose faithfulness and kindnesses we live, and Esther, the partner of our kingdom, together with her entire nation;
verses.16:14: intending this: that once they were killed, he might lay an ambush against our isolation and transfer the kingdom of the Persians to the Macedonians.
verses.16:15: We, however, have found the Jews, who were marked for slaughter by the worst of mortals, in no fault at all, but on the contrary making use of just laws,
verses.16:16: and sons of the Most High and greatest and ever-living God, by whose kindness the kingdom was handed down both to our fathers and to us, and is guarded to this very day.
verses.16:17: Therefore, know that those letters which he had sent out under our name are void.
verses.16:18: For which crime, before the gates of this city, that is, Susa, both he himself who schemed it and all his kindred hang on gallows, with not us, but God repaying him what he deserved.
verses.16:19: Now let this edict, which we are now sending, be posted in all the cities, so that it may be permitted for the Jews to follow their own laws.
verses.16:20: To them you must be a support, so that they may be able to put to death those who had prepared themselves for their slaughter on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is called Adar.
verses.16:21: For this day of grief and mourning, almighty God has turned into joy for them.
verses.16:22: Therefore you too shall keep this day among the other festive days, and celebrate it with all gladness, so that even in the future it may be known
verses.16:23: that all who faithfully obey the Persians receive a worthy reward for their loyalty, whereas those who plot against their kingdom perish for their crime.
verses.16:24: Now let every province and city that refuses to share in this observance perish by sword and fire, and be so destroyed that it becomes impassable forever not only to humans, but even to beasts, as an example of contempt and disobedience."

notes.1:1: Stage 1 restored the canonical Clementine Vulgate opening (Esther 1:1) here; Mordecai's dream opening (previously placed at 1:1 to mirror Greek Addition A) belongs at its native Vulgate position in 11:2.
notes.1:2: Vulgate exordium ('beginning') distinctively renders the Hebrew phrase for 'Susa the citadel' (habbirah), presenting Susa as the starting seat of the king's realm.
notes.1:6: Vulgate eburneis circulis ('ivory rings') differs from the Hebrew 'silver rings', and smaragdino et pario lapide ('emerald and Parian stone') freely renders the Hebrew list of precious paving stones.
notes.1:10: Vulgate post nimiam potationem incaluisset mero ('after excessive drinking had grown warm with unmixed wine') expands the Hebrew 'when the heart of the king was merry with wine'.
notes.1:18: Vulgate unde regis justa est indignatio ('therefore the indignation of the king is just') differs notably from the Hebrew 'and there will be plenty of contempt and wrath'.
notes.2:5: Vulgate de stirpe Jemini ('of the lineage of Jemini') preserves the Hebrew gentilic yemini ('a Benjaminite') as an ancestral name, contrasting with de tribu Benjamin in 1:1.
notes.2:9: Vulgate praecepit eunucho ('he commanded a eunuch') has Hegai delegate Esther's care to a subordinate eunuch, whereas the Hebrew describes Hegai himself hastening to provide her cosmetics and portions.
notes.2:15: The closing sentence ('For she was exceedingly lovely and of incredible beauty; to the eyes of all she appeared gracious and lovable') is a distinctive Vulgate expansion of the briefer Hebrew statement that Esther won favor in the sight of all who saw her.
notes.2:17: Vulgate repeats mulieres ('women') in both clauses, whereas the Hebrew has 'women' in the first clause and 'virgins' in the second.
notes.3:2: Vulgate uses Roman imperial terminology here, calling the king imperator ('emperor') and using adorabant ('paid homage to') for court prostration.
notes.3:7: Vulgate distinctively adds in urnam ('into an urn') and specifies 'as to what day and what month the Jewish people should be killed', where the Hebrew describes casting the lot from day to day and month to month.
notes.3:8: Vulgate characterizes Jewish practices as 'new' (novis, where the Hebrew has 'different from every people') and adds the warning against growing 'insolent through license' (ut insolescat per licentiam).
notes.3:15: Vulgate concludes with 'all the Jews who were in the city were weeping' (flentibus), whereas the Hebrew states that the city of Susa was thrown into confusion.
notes.4:3: The Vulgate expands the Hebrew ("in every province, the place where the king's word and law arrived") by adding "towns, and places" (oppidis, ac locis) and calling the decree "cruel" (crudele).
notes.4:8: Latin pendebat literally means "was hanging" (that is, publicly posted), whereas the Hebrew reads "had been given."
notes.4:11: The Vulgate adds "as a sign of clemency" (pro signo clementiae) and the emphatic "immediately without any delay" (absque ulla cunctatione statim), neither of which has a direct equivalent in the Hebrew.
notes.4:14: Distinctively in the Vulgate, deliverance comes "through another opportunity" (per aliam occasionem, vs. Hebrew "from another place") and the closing clause adds the verb "that you might be prepared at such a time" (ut in tali tempore parareris, vs. Hebrew "for such a time as this").
notes.4:16: The Vulgate introduces an explicit call to prayer (orate pro me, "pray for me," where the Hebrew has "fast for me") and replaces the Hebrew "if I perish, I perish" with "handing myself over to death and danger" (tradensque me morti et periculo).
notes.5:1: Jerome uses Roman imperial architectural terms here: basilica ("hall") for the royal building and consistorium ("council chamber") for the king's formal audience hall.
notes.5:2: Latin virgam auream ('golden scepter', matching 4:11 and 8:4) and osculata est summitatem virgae ejus ('kissed the tip of his scepter', whereas the Hebrew reads 'touched the tip of the scepter') are distinctive Vulgate details restored in Stage 1.
notes.5:6: Where the Hebrew reads "at the banquet of wine," the Vulgate renders "after he had drunk wine abundantly" (postquam vinum biberat abundanter).
notes.5:8: Instead of the Hebrew "tomorrow I will do according to the word of the king," the Vulgate has Esther promise, "tomorrow I will reveal my will to the king" (aperiam regi voluntatem meam).
notes.5:14: For the single Hebrew noun denoting the wooden execution structure ("tree/wood"), the Vulgate employs two distinct Latin terms here, first trabs ("beam") and then crux ("cross"), and later patibulum ("gallows") in 6:4.
notes.6:2: The Vulgate spells the first eunuch's name Bagathan (matching Bigthan in 2:21 rather than Hebrew Bigthana here) and renders "sought to lay hands on" with the vivid verb jugulare (lit. "to cut the throat of").
notes.6:4: Distinctively in the Vulgate, Haman enters "the inner courtyard" (interius atrium), whereas the Hebrew specifies the outer court.
notes.6:8: Latin qui de sella regis est (lit. "that is of the king's saddle") idiomatically denotes a horse the king himself rides. Moreover, the Vulgate explicitly places the royal diadem on the honored man's head (super caput suum), whereas the Hebrew syntax places it on the horse's head.
notes.6:11: While the Hebrew repeats the exact proclamation of 6:9, the Vulgate varies Haman's cry here to Hoc honore condignus est ("Worthy of this honor is...").
notes.7:2: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew "at the banquet of wine" as "after he had grown warm with wine" (postquam vino incaluerat).
notes.7:4: The Vulgate reads "we have been handed over" (traditi sumus, versus Hebrew "sold"), expands Esther's lament with "it would be a bearable evil, and, groaning," and renders the difficult final Hebrew clause as "whose cruelty rebounds upon the king" (cujus crudelitas redundat in regem).
notes.7:5: Where the Hebrew asks "and where is he," the Vulgate asks "and of what power is he" (cujus potentiæ).
notes.7:9: Across these chapters the Vulgate uses three distinct terms for the instrument of execution: "timber" (lignum) here, "gallows" (patibulum) in 7:10 and 9:13, and "cross" (crux) in 8:7 and 9:25.
notes.8:1: The Vulgate explicitly identifies Mordecai as Esther's paternal uncle (patruus, matching Vulgate 2:7, 15), whereas the Hebrew says only that she told the king what Mordecai was to her.
notes.8:7: The Vulgate employs Roman crucifixion language, "fastened to a cross" (affigi cruci; cf. 9:25), where the Hebrew says "hanged on the wood."
notes.8:8: The second sentence shifts in the Vulgate to third-person past-tense narration ("For this was the custom... sealed with his ring") explaining Persian royal protocol, rather than continuing the king's direct speech as in the Hebrew.
notes.8:10: Instead of listing breeds of royal horses as in the Hebrew, the Vulgate supplies a purpose clause stating that the couriers were to forestall the old letters with new messages.
notes.8:15: The Vulgate describes Mordecai's royal garments as "violet and sky-blue" (hyacinthinis... et æriis, for aeriis) and his cloak as "silk" (serico), where the Hebrew has "blue and white" and "fine linen."
notes.9:5: In the Latin, the reflexive pronoun refers back to the Jews, the subject of the main clause.
notes.9:6: The Vulgate introduces Haman's ten sons here as an addition to the five hundred killed ("besides the ten sons of Haman... whose names are these"), restructuring the sequence of verses 6-10 in the Hebrew.
notes.9:9: The Vulgate reads "Jezatha," omitting the initial syllable of the Hebrew name "Vaizatha."
notes.9:26: The Vulgate adds that the lot was cast "into the urn" (in urnam) and explicitly glosses "this letter" with "that is, of this book" (epistolæ, id est, libri hujus volumine).
notes.9:32: Where the Hebrew closes with Esther's decree confirming Purim and its recording in the book, the Vulgate continues the list from verse 31 and explicitly names "this book, which is called Esther."
notes.10:1: The Vulgate adds "entire" (omnem) and "all" (cunctas) and reads "made ... subject to tribute" (fecit tributarias), where the Hebrew MT has "laid a tribute on the land and the coastlands of the sea."
notes.10:2: The Vulgate gives a declarative statement ("are written") citing the plural "books of the Medes and Persians" and the "honor and eminence" with which the king exalted Mordecai, whereas the Hebrew MT poses a rhetorical question citing "the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia."
notes.10:3: In native Clementine Vulgate versification, 10:3 concludes the canonical Hebrew-based narrative, while Mordecai's interpretation of his dream (Addition F) follows as 10:4-13 (mapped to Saints.Bible 10:3 in parallel display).
notes.10:4: Verses 10:4-13 preserve Mordecai's interpretation of his dream (Addition F) at its native Vulgate position (parallel to Saints.Bible 10:3).
notes.10:10: Vulgate praecepit ('commanded') is a distinctive Latin rendering.
notes.10:11: Vulgate in statutum ex illo jam tempore diem coram Deo universis gentibus ('to the day already fixed from that time before God for all the nations') uses the prepositionless dative universis gentibus.
notes.11:1: In native Clementine Vulgate order, chapters 11-16 gather the Greek-derived Additions translated by Jerome at the end of the book; 11:1 is the Purim colophon (Addition F, end of Greek 10:3), while 11:2 begins Addition A.
notes.11:2: Relocated from old English 1:1 to its native Clementine Vulgate position at 11:2 (Addition A; mapped to Saints.Bible 1:1). In the Additions (11:2, 12:2, 13:1, 16:1), the Vulgate names the king Artaxerxes rather than Ahasuerus (Assuerus). Final period changed to colon to match Latin punctuation introducing 11:3.
notes.11:10: The adopted Clementine text reads creavit (a Clementine textual variant/form for crevit, 'grew', as in 10:6); rendered 'grew' in keeping with the Latin syntax in fluvium maximum.
notes.12:1: Latin Bagatha and Thara reflect the Greek-derived forms of the two eunuchs' names in Addition A (corresponding to Bigthan and Teresh in 2:21).
notes.12:6: Vulgate Bugaeus preserves the Addition A epithet (cf. 'of the lineage of Agag' in 3:1 and 'Macedonian' in 16:10). The final two sentences are Jerome's editorial bridge repeating the close of 3:13 to anchor Artaxerxes's first decree (chapter 13, Addition B).
notes.13:4: Latin novis ... legibus literally means 'new' or 'strange/unusual laws.'
notes.13:6: Vulgate 13:6 specifies the fourteenth day of Adar (quartadecima die), whereas 3:13 and 16:20 specify the thirteenth.
notes.13:7: Latin ad inferos ('to the underworld') uses the edition's standard rendering. The closing sentence repeats 4:17 as Jerome's editorial bridge anchoring Mordecai's and Esther's prayers (13:8-14:19, Addition C).
notes.13:12: Latin adorarem ('bow down before' or 'worship', repeated in 13:14) carries both courtly prostration and religious worship.
notes.13:17: Latin funiculo tuo literally means 'Your measuring cord/line,' a biblical idiom for an allotted inheritance.
notes.14:16: Latin in diebus silentii mei literally means 'in the days of my silence' (i.e., private seclusion).
notes.15:1: The parenthetical (haud dubium quin esset Mardochæus) is Jerome's explicit editorial gloss preserved in the Clementine Vulgate introducing Addition D.
notes.15:4: The Clementine Vulgate literally reads vestimenta ornatus sui ('her garments of adornment', a historic Vulgate form where 'garments of her prayer/service' is expected in context), contrasting with circumdata est gloria sua ('was clothed with her glory').
notes.15:16: Latin domine ('my lord') is lowercase as courtly address to the king (also in 15:17).
notes.16:5: Latin mendaciorum cuniculis ('by tunnels of lies') uses the military image of subterranean sapping/mining.
